0.original: Alisaie would share the findings of your scouting mission with everyone.

48.original: Soon after you left, who should arrive in Amity but Urianger and the Exarch. I'm glad they were able to find you.

49.original: I'm told you went ahead to scout out the volcano. I don't suppose some grappling hooks will suffice?

50.original: A-All that grinding and shaking... I-I was afraid the lift floor would fall out from underneath me...

51.original: B-But don't worry! I-I'm sure the trembling will go away s-soon!

52.original: Thus are we all gathered...though Ryne, I am afeared, did not much enjoy the ascent.

53.original: Forgive us our delay. The Exarch arrived and we took some time to apprise him of our mission.

54.original: ...Concerned for my health, are you? Indeed, we are a little far from the Crystarium, but rest assured this old man can muster up another wind for what is to come.

55.original: Oh, don't mind us. We're just taking in the sights.

56.original: Ahhh, such an exhilarating ride! And such a magnificent view! Nothing in Eulmore compares to this!

57.original: Shall we see how we might be of service?

58.original: When he asked for my hand, my husband promised that he would one day build a Talos that could take us to the very heavens. And now he'll do it!

59.original: Have the design ready, she says! In good time, she says! Does she even understand what's involved!?

60.original: Before I can even attempt to design anything, I need intimate knowledge of the land─the knowledge of locals. Last I heard, no one lives here!

61.original: What? A village of Eulmoran exiles!?

62.original: B-But...those people have every reason to loathe a free citizen like me! They couldn't possibly be willing to cooperate!

63.original: <sob> This will never work. <hex:021A020203>Never<hex:021A020103>. I never should've fixed that ruddy lift. Never should've ridden it up here... Never should've...never should've...

64.original: I can't do it... It's impossible...

65.original: Oh dear, darling appears to have lost the plot...

66.original: But he has it in him, <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>. He's the cleverest man I know─he just wants for confidence sometimes. If you were to give him some words of encouragement, I'm sure he can give you your Talos.

67.original: A bit of advice I learned from his mother: he responds poorly to obvious praise. You'll need to find another way to stoke the fires of his motivation─awaken his sense of daring!

68.original: Choose words that will best encourage Chai-Nuzz.

69.original: In order to succeed, you must lift his spirits sufficiently during the conversation.

76.original: I can't do it. No one can. A Talos of that size...no one's even dreamed of it.

78.original: Alphinaud once struggled to collect firewood.

79.original: Dulia is counting on you as well.

80.original: You're a genius! You can do this!

81.original: He did? But...he's such a capable lad, brimming with confidence.

82.original: Hmmm... I suppose even the most capable among us have struggles to overcome...

83.original: But regardless of my own feelings, I can't do a damn thing without help from those villagers...and they're not bally likely to give it!

84.original: I know, I know! You hardly need to tell me that! Do you think I'd disappoint her if I could help it!?

85.original: But regardless of my own feelings, I can't do a damn thing without help from those villagers...and they're not bally likely to give it!

86.original: Oh, it's simple as that, is it? You say some magic words and I can suddenly do the impossible? Don't make me laugh!

87.original: As I said, I can't do a damn thing without help from those villagers...and they're not bally likely to give it!

88.original: Tristol's among them, you said so yourself! Lest you've forgotten, we essentially sent him to his death! Even if the others don't bear a personal grudge, <hex:021A020203>he<hex:021A020103> would never forgive us!

90.original: You don't know until you apologize. I'll come with you.

91.original: Don't worry! He'll forgive you for sure!

92.original: Things won't improve by themselves. You have to take the first step.

93.original: Hmmm... If you were there too, perhaps he'd be more willing to accept an apology...

94.original: W-Wait... What am I thinking, relying on others to fight my battles? It's disgraceful, is what it is, and it might even make things worse...

95.original: And in the end, it's not even a question of forgiveness. Building such an enormous Talos is impossible, and no amount of contrition will change that!

96.original: How can you make such blithe claims without proof? You're either naive or you think I am─and I most certainly am not!

97.original: And whatever you say, in the end it's not even a question of forgiveness. Building such an enormous Talos is impossible, and no amount of contrition will change that!

98.original: I know, I know... Unless we take the first step, there can never be reconciliation.

99.original: This is a chance for everyone to come together. Even if they hurled stones at me, perhaps it's worth trying to apologize...

100.original: But what then? In the end, it's not even a question of forgiveness. Building such an enormous Talos is impossible, and no amount of contrition will change that.

101.original: And even if by some miracle the people of Amity were willing to let bygones be bygones, they'd think that the plan is absurd! <hex:021A020203>I<hex:021A020103> think it's absurd!

103.original: It's less absurd than the change that's come to Eulmore.

104.original: We liberated a castle with a strategy that many would call absurd.

105.original: Everything you touch turns to gold! No one would doubt your plan!

106.original: Well, I can't argue with that logic... Enormous as the task is, it's simply a matter of finding a solution to a practical problem. From that perspective, it's not entirely unrealistic.

107.original: But realistic or no, there's no guarantee of success. There are risks to consider should the venture fail.

108.original: Well now, to flood the very castle you sought to reclaim... Such a strategy could indeed be considered absurd. Yet you succeeded not in spite of, but because of it.

109.original: Our own strategy may likewise seem absurd, but maybe─just maybe it stands a better chance of success for it...

110.original: But be that as it may, there are risks to consider should the venture fail.

111.original: I've no idea where that absolute confidence of yours comes from, but it only makes me feel more wary!

112.original: And even assuming there's a semblance of realism to the plan, have you considered the risks should the venture fail?

113.original: Aye, imagine for a moment that we fail to reach Vauthry and only succeed in provoking him. In his fury, he may well unleash his hordes of eaters and we'll meet a horrible end!

116.original: I'll protect you. I'll protect everyone.

117.original: We could build Talos for battle.

118.original: Oh, so I can die with you!? How very kind of you to offer! But if it's all the same, I'd rather keep on living!

119.original: <sigh> How can you remain so...so <hex:021A020203>optimistic<hex:021A020103> throughout all this? It's downright tiring...

121.original: I-I see what you did there. That's how you win over the masses─with that irrepressible aura of dependability.

122.original: But very well, you've made your conviction clear...and I'm assured in spite of myself. I won't let my fears get the better of me. It's unseemly if nothing else.

123.original: Still, I find it astounding that you can have such certainty given the circumstances.

124.original: I've thought of that, I assure you, but I'm afraid Talos cannot contend with sin eaters. If they could, I would never have come to Eulmore.

125.original: Nonetheless, I appreciate your earnest attempt to find a solution.

126.original: It makes me wonder, what is it that drives you?

127.original: Tell me, why did you throw yourself into the midst of such a grueling struggle?

133.original: Indeed... What else could compel us to face such dangers? I too have someone I wish to protect, with whom I want to live out my days in peace...

134.original: Adventure... Such a strange word coming from my lips... I used to have a sense of adventure too. Strove to challenge myself. Whenever did I lose it?

135.original: So you do not fight willingly. Just like me. We may put on a smile, but behind it there's only doubt. If even your heart isn't in it, there's no hope for any of us. No point in building the Talos.

136.original: You failed to encourage Chai-Nuzz. Speak with Dulia-Chai to try again.

137.original: Yes... Yes! By the gods, I can do this! I just need to have a little faith in myself!

138.original: Right, let's head to Amity and speak with the villagers─with Tristol.

139.original: My love, things are liable to become more dangerous. I want you to wait for me back in Eulmore.

140.original: No. Wherever you go, I'm going too.

141.original: Besides...you're not the only one who has to apologize.

142.original: B-But there's no telling what may happen out here! I don't know if I can keep you safe!

143.original: P-Perhaps this is a bad idea after all... I-I don't think I have what it takes...

144.original: Master Chai. That you are beset with doubt is proof that you can envision the task ahead.

145.original: And that which man can envision, he can make reality. Thus did some old friends of mine once say.

146.original: Even should it be a feat fit for the divine, if something has been done before, then it most assuredly can be done again by our own hands.

147.original: That's a little idealistic, don't you think!?

148.original: Perhaps, Master Chai, perhaps. But what is man if not an idealistic creature?

149.original: 'Tis not an easy thing to achieve one's dreams─my friends can attest to that. Countless times did they meet with frustration in the course of their endeavors.

150.original: None would have found fault with them had they given up, yet they never did. One step after the next, they forged on towards their goals.

151.original: And for their determination, they accomplished numerous feats that many believed lay beyond the reach of mankind.

152.original: Like them, you are a man of science. Amidst your doubts, surely there is a spark of desire. The desire to make the impossible possible.

153.original: Come, darling. Like the old days, I would be the first to see your Talos.

154.original: And you shall be, my dear. I would have none other at my side when my greatest masterpiece awakens.

156.original: I am glad my words struck a chord. Shall we?

158.original: You have every right to be angry with us. But please listen to what I have to say.

159.original: I am tasked with delivering these people to Mt. Gulg─by means of a Talos of heretofore unseen proportions.

160.original: However, I cannot do this without the cooperation of those with intimate knowledge of this land. That is, you and your fellow villagers.

161.original: ...Cooperation? After you ignored my desperate pleas and cast me out, you have the gall to come here and ask for my cooperation?

162.original: You've every right to be upset. Vauthry's not the one to blame for your suffering─we are.

163.original: We were free citizens without a care in the world, indifferent to the hardship of others. We didn't know what would become of you, and frankly, we didn't care.

164.original: But we know now that what we did to you─to full many─was wrong. Terribly wrong. No words will suffice to make amends, but I want you to know that we are deeply sorry.

165.original: I'm not sure how I feel.

166.original: Should I forgive you? Hate you? Perhaps it's not even my place to judge. After all, I sought a place in your city. I wanted to be you, once...

167.original: But one thing is clear to me.

168.original: All of that is in the past. And we mustn't let past wrongs stand in the way of a brighter future.

169.original: And so...I will cooperate with you. Please see our friends to Mt. Gulg.

171.original: I'll set to work on the design at once. Wouldn't do to have nothing to show the others when they return with help.

172.original: Make no mistake, this venture is unprecedented in the history of Talos building─nay, the history of all mankind! But rest assured this genius of Daedalus Stoneworks will deliver!

175.original: Well...er, you see... I've been promised people to procure the stone as well as imbue magic.

176.original: When I was put on the spot earlier, I thought that was all we required.

177.original: But I forgot about one rather important item needed to bring a Talos to life...

181.original: That's right, the heart! I'm pleased to see you have some familiarity with Talos!

182.original: The heart! The godsdamned, bally heart! Without one, a Talos is just a hunk of rock!

183.original: So, while I work on the design, I'd be much obliged if you could see to procuring the ore with which to fashion a heart.

184.original: A heart suitable of bringing to life a Talos that shall embrace the very firmament!
